2608.27127.title: TransMeme: A Multi-Agent Framework for Cross-Cultural Meme Transcreation
2608.27127.paper_summary: Internet memes are a pervasive form of multimodal online communication; however, such communication often involves users from diverse linguistic and cultural backgrounds. Therefore, adapting memes across cultures and languages is a central challenge for enabling mutual understanding in online communication. Unlike ordinary translation or standalone text rewriting, cross-cultural meme transcreation must jointly preserve communicative intent, adapt culture-dependent meaning for the target audience, and maintain coherence between text and image. In this work, we first provide an explicit task analysis of cross-cultural meme transcreation and identify three core challenges: culture-specific knowledge understanding, intent and tone preservation, and multimodal consistency. Based on this analysis, we propose a multi-agent framework with specialized agents that are coordinated to address these challenges through cultural adaptation, target text rewriting, revision, and conditional visual adjustment. The framework strengthens target text adaptation with coordinated feedback to handle difficult cases that require deeper cultural or visual intervention. We evaluate the framework on bidirectional Chinese-English meme transcreation using both human evaluation and LLM-as-a-Judge. Our method consistently outperforms all baselines across both evaluation settings. In human evaluation, it achieves the best performance on all four dimensions and delivers a 33.1% average improvement over the strongest baseline, while in LLM-as-a-Judge, it attains the highest Top-1 ranking rate (60% versus 26% for the second-best baseline). Further analysis indicates that each component contributes to the performance. Our error analysis suggests that the remaining bottlenecks lie in humor reconstruction and image-text alignment rather than simple cultural knowledge gaps, pointing to future work on humor transfer.
2608.27127.paper_summary_zh: 網路迷因是一種普遍存在的多模態線上溝通形式；然而，這種溝通通常涉及來自不同語言和文化背景的使用者。<lb/>因此，跨文化和語言的迷因適應是促進線上溝通中相互理解的一個核心挑戰。<lb/>與普通翻譯或獨立文本重寫不同，跨文化迷因再創作必須共同保留溝通意圖，為目標受眾調整文化依賴的意義，並保持文本與圖像之間的一致性。<lb/>在這項工作中，我們首先提供了跨文化迷因再創作的明確任務分析，並確定了三個核心挑戰：文化特定知識理解、意圖和語調保留，以及多模態一致性。<lb/>基於這一分析，我們提出了一個多代理框架，具有專門的代理，這些代理協調合作以通過文化適應、目標文本重寫、修訂和條件視覺調整來解決這些挑戰。<lb/>該框架通過協調反饋來加強目標文本的適應，以處理需要更深入文化或視覺介入的困難案例。<lb/>我們在雙向中英文迷因再創作上評估了該框架，使用了人類評估和LLM-as-a-Judge。<lb/>我們的方法在兩種評估設置中始終超越所有基準。<lb/>在人工評估中，它在所有四個維度上達到了最佳表現，並在最強基準上實現了33.1%的平均改進，而在LLM-as-a-Judge中，它達到了最高的Top-1排名率（60%對比第二強基準的26%）。<lb/>進一步分析表明，每個組件對性能都有貢獻。<lb/>我們的錯誤分析表明，剩餘的瓶頸在於幽默重建和圖像文本對齊，而非簡單的文化知識差距，這指向了未來在幽默轉移上的工作。
